title: Fibre products of qcqs algebraic spaces are qcqs
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $A,B,C$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $f:A\to C$ and $g:B\to C$ be morphisms. Suppose each of $A,B,C$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Here quasi-compact means that every open covering of the underlying point space, with the topology of [def-a1-space-point-topology], has a finite subcover; quasi-separated means that the absolute diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests, equivalently that $T\times_ZT'$ is quasi-compact for every two affine schemes mapping to $Z$, for each space $Z$ under consideration. A morphism of spaces is quasi-compact on scheme tests if its base change by any affine scheme has quasi-compact source. Then the algebraic-space fibre product $A\times_CB$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. No quasi-compactness or separation assumption is imposed on the ambient scheme $S$.

source.place: Tag 073B, lemma-quasi-compact-quasi-separated-permanence, clause (3), with the base space C assumed qcqs as in its proof.

proof.text: First reconcile the two quasi-compactness conventions used by the cited nodes. A space with quasi-compact point space has an affine surjective etale atlas by [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas]; conversely a quasi-compact scheme atlas gives quasi-compact point space by [lem-a1-space-finite-affine-subatlas]. For a morphism $h:E\to F$ satisfying the affine-scheme test and any quasi-compact algebraic space $W\to F$, choose an affine surjective etale atlas $V\to W$. Then $E\times_FV$ is quasi-compact by the affine test, and $E\times_FV\to E\times_FW$ is surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Its point map is continuous and surjective by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. The continuous-surjection clause of [lem-a1-space-finite-affine-subatlas] therefore makes $E\times_FW$ quasi-compact. The converse follows by choosing $W$ affine. Thus the affine-test notion equals the quasi-compact-space-test notion, also for diagonals.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence] to $f:A\to C$. Its hypotheses are exactly that $A$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $C$ is quasi-separated, so $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. In particular its relative diagonal $\Delta_f:A\to A\times_CA$ is quasi-compact on affine scheme tests.

Let $P=A\times_CB$ and $p:P\to B$; this is an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. For every affine scheme $T\to B$, transitivity identifies $P\times_BT$ with $A\times_CT$, so $p$ is quasi-compact by the affine test for $f$. The square with top map $\Delta_p:P\to P\times_BP$, bottom map $\Delta_f:A\to A\times_CA$, and vertical maps forgetting the $B$ coordinate is cartesian: a pair $((a_1,b),(a_2,b))$ belongs to the diagonal precisely when $a_1=a_2$. Consequently, for every affine $T\to P\times_BP$ there is an isomorphism
$$T\times_{P\times_BP}P\cong T\times_{A\times_CA}A.$$
The right-hand side is quasi-compact since $\Delta_f$ is. Thus $\Delta_p$ is quasi-compact, and $p$ is quasi-separated. These identities are identities of fibre-product functors on scheme sections, not claims about fibre products of point spaces.
Since $p$ is quasi-compact and $B$ is quasi-compact, the quasi-compact-space-test formulation established in step 1, applied to $B\xrightarrow{1}B$, shows that $P\times_BB\cong P$ is quasi-compact.

Apply only the first assertion of [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-source-products] to $p:P\to B$: its target $B$ is absolutely quasi-separated by hypothesis, and $p$ is quasi-separated by step 3. Hence $P$ is absolutely quasi-separated. This assertion is about the absolute algebraic spaces (over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$) underlying our $S$-spaces, exactly the absolute convention of the item; it does not require that $S$ be quasi-separated. Together with step 4 this proves the claim. The separate fibre-product assertion of the cited node is not used.
